title: Exchange of the trace maps: evaluation and support
statement:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] (no Cartesian leg square, no properness
over $s$), with the notation and admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Then:

1. *(evaluation)* as maps $Rq_*P_X\to R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
\delta_{K'}\circ\rho_f=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\delta_K ;
$$
1. *(support)* as maps
$Rg_*Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}=Ri_{b*}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\to Rb^!R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
Rb^!\bigl(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\bigr)\circ\mathsf E\circ Rg_*\zeta_c
=\zeta_b\circ Ri_{b*}\tau_h ,
$$
where the source identification is $gi_c=i_bh$.

Moreover, for a Cartesian square $(\beta',\alpha',\beta,\alpha)$
($\beta:V\to W$, $\alpha:U\to W$ proper, $V'=V\times_WU$) the exceptional
adjoint of the right-adjoint base-change isomorphism
$R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\beta^!R\alpha_*$ (the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$) is
$R\beta_!R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\alpha_!R\beta'_!R\beta'^!
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}R\alpha_*$, the composition law followed by the
counit of $\beta'$.

proof.text:
Work at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ inherited from [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with the constructible exceptional adjoints of [def-trf-admissibility]. The concrete operation package [prop-functor-package] supplies the proper identifications, compact-support composition, projection and exchange maps on these domains. In particular no ambient exceptional adjoint, and no properness of a structure morphism, is used. We use the adjunction-compatible exceptional composition comparison: the right adjoint of $Rv_!Ru_!$ is $Ru^!Rv^!$, since its Hom bijection is the composite of the two adjunction bijections. Conjugating the compact-support composition isomorphism as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives $R(vu)^!\cong Ru^!Rv^!$. Applied to the identity of $Ru^!Rv^!N$, the two inverse Hom bijections give the counit
$$\varepsilon_{vu,N}=\varepsilon_{v,N}\circ Rv_!(\varepsilon_{u,Rv^!N}).$$
This also checks its normalization: the two units and counits in the conjugation formula cancel by the triangle identities. Associativity of the left composition comparisons [thm-sf-comp-composition] implies associativity of their conjugates, because conjugation reverses composition. These are assertions about the specified constructible adjunctions, so the stronger ambient hypothesis in some older mate lemmas is unnecessary.

source.place: Preliminaries for the last assertion and support: pasted exceptional counits

proof.text:
For the last assertion put $T=\operatorname{Ex}_!:L\alpha^*R\beta_!\to R\beta'_!L\alpha'^*$, and let
$$\Theta:R\beta_!R\alpha'_* = R\beta_!R\alpha'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\alpha_!R\beta'_! = R\alpha_*R\beta'_!$$
be composition along $\beta\alpha'=\alpha\beta'$. The primed proper identification is legitimate by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The compatibility of exchange with composition and square morphisms [fix-lem-exchanges], applied to the ordinary counit of $\alpha'$, gives the following explicit normalization, with all comparisons inserted:
$$\varepsilon_\alpha\circ L\alpha^*\Theta
=R\beta'_!\varepsilon_{\alpha'}\circ T R\alpha'_*.
\tag{*}$$
Here the left side has source $L\alpha^*R\beta_!R\alpha'_*$ and target $R\beta'_!$. To see the normalization directly, use the unit--square--counit formula of [def-exchange-projection] for each proper factor in a compactification of $\beta$, paste the composition comparisons, and take the $L\alpha^*\dashv R\alpha_*$ transpose. The square comparisons identify the two pullback composites. Naturality moves the counit of $\alpha'$ past that identification; the remaining pair $R\alpha'_*\varepsilon_{\alpha'}\circ\eta_{\alpha'}R\alpha'_*$ is the identity. For the open factor write $\beta=j$, $\beta'=j'$. The comparison $\Theta=\gamma:j_!R\alpha'_*\to R\alpha_*j'_!$ is the properly normalized proper/open comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. For an object $Z$ on the upper left corner put
$$e=\operatorname{Ex}_{*,\alpha}(j'_!Z):j^*R\alpha_*j'_!Z\longrightarrow R\alpha'_*Z.$$
The normalization of $\gamma$ by the canonical sheaf identification gives
$$e\circ j^*\gamma_Z=\mathrm{id}_{R\alpha'_*Z};$$
indeed restricting the representative $j_!\alpha'_*J\cong\alpha_*j'_!J\to\alpha_*I$ of that lemma to $j$ gives precisely the inverse proper-base-change identification $e^{-1}$. The unit--square--counit formula of [def-exchange-projection] gives
$$j'^*\varepsilon_{\alpha,j'_!Z}
=\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z}\circ\alpha'^*e.$$
Also the open base-change map $\alpha^*j_!\cong j'_!\alpha'^*$ restricts to the identity on the open, by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. Hence restricting the two sides of (*) to $j'$ gives, on the left,
$$\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z}\circ\alpha'^*(e\circ j^*\gamma_Z)
=\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z},$$
and on the right $\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z}$. This proves (*) for the open factor: its source is $j'_!\alpha'^*R\alpha'_*Z$; maps from that source are determined by their restriction, using the derived adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-derived-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and the unit isomorphism of [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-fully-faithful], which remains an isomorphism degreewise on complexes. Take the coefficient category there to be $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$. The proper arrows in this open square are the appropriate base changes of $\alpha$. At finite coefficients its bounded-below etale statement transports to the witnessed pro-etale operations in the coefficient conventions of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Compactification/refinement independence and compatibility with composition are exactly item (4) of [fix-lem-exchanges]. This argument compares $T$ with $\Theta$; it never identifies the compact-support and ordinary exchange for the nonproper map $\beta$.

Let $B:R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\to R\beta^!R\alpha_*$ be the conjugate of $T$. By the conjugation formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], its $R\beta_!\dashv R\beta^!$ adjoint has $L\alpha^*\dashv R\alpha_*$ transpose
$$\varepsilon_{\beta'}\circ R\beta'_!\varepsilon_{\alpha'}\circ T R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!.$$
The candidate $R\alpha_*\varepsilon_{\beta'}\circ\Theta R\beta'^!$ has the same transpose by (*) and counit naturality. The two adjunction bijections are injective, proving the last assertion. Invertibility of $B$ is conjugation of the base-change isomorphism, as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

source.place: The last assertion: explicit double transpose and counit normalization

proof.text:
Write $L=D_XK$. For proper $f$, the inverse $\Pi_f$ of the specified $!$-Künneth map satisfies
$$\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\Pi_f=\varepsilon_f\boxtimes\varepsilon_f:
q^*(Rf_*K\boxtimes Rf_*L)\longrightarrow K\boxtimes L.\tag{**}$$
Here is the counit calculation with the product factors specified. Put $B=Y\times_sY$, $U=X\times_sY$, $V=Y\times_sX$, $T=X\times_sX$, and write $a=f\times1:U\to B$, $b=1\times f:V\to B$, $r=1\times f:T\to U$, $t=f\times1:T\to V$; thus $ar=bt=q$. These four arrows are base changes of the proper $f$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Put $M=\operatorname{pr}_X^*K$ on $U$, $N=\operatorname{pr}_X^*L$ on $V$, $H=Ra_*M$, and $J=Rb_*N$. Proper base change identifies $H\otimes J$ with $Rf_*K\boxtimes Rf_*L$ and $r^*M\otimes t^*N$ with $K\boxtimes L$. By [def-sf-kv-maps](i) and the exact composite specified in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative], $\Pi_f$ is, under these identifications,
$$
\begin{aligned}
H\otimes J
&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_b^{\mathrm{sym}}}
Rb_*(b^*H\otimes N)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rb_*(\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a}\otimes1)}
Rb_*(Rt_*r^*M\otimes N)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rb_*\operatorname{PF}_t}
Rb_*Rt_*(r^*M\otimes t^*N)
\cong Rq_*(K\boxtimes L).
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $\operatorname{PF}_b^{\mathrm{sym}}$ means symmetry, $\operatorname{PF}_{b,N,H}$, and the image of symmetry. The proper projection maps are the counit-defined maps of [def-exchange-projection], by the proper compatibility of [fix-prop-projection-formula]. Their transposes are respectively $1\otimes\varepsilon_{b,N}$ and $\varepsilon_{t,r^*M}\otimes1$. The transpose of the middle exchange is
$$t^*b^*Ra_*M=r^*a^*Ra_*M\xrightarrow{r^*\varepsilon_{a,M}}r^*M,$$
by the unit--square--counit formula in [def-exchange-projection]. Consequently, transposing the displayed composite first along $b$ and then along $t$ gives
$$t^*b^*(H\otimes J)\longrightarrow
r^*M\otimes t^*N,\qquad
r^*\varepsilon_{a,M}\otimes t^*\varepsilon_{b,N}.$$
The units inserted by the two projection maps and the exchange cancel by the ordinary triangle identities [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). The unconditional ordinary part of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) identifies this iterated transpose with $\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\Pi_f$. Under the two proper-base-change identifications defining $H,J$, the unit--square--counit formula identifies these two factors with $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\varepsilon_f$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2^*\varepsilon_f$. This proves (**). Only the composition, projection and base-change clauses of the relative Künneth theorem are used; their concrete finite-coefficient domains and proper comparisons were supplied in step 1. All inputs, including $L=D_XK$, are in the bounded constructible finite-Tor category by [prop-functor-package](7).

source.place: Evaluation, the claim: transpose of the specified inverse Künneth map

proof.text:
The diagonal square $q\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$ is merely commutative. Define its ordinary exchange $\mathrm{Ex}:\Delta_Y^*Rq_*\to Rf_*\Delta_X^*$ by the general mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: its $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ transpose is
$$f^*\Delta_Y^*Rq_*=\Delta_X^*q^*Rq_*\xrightarrow{\Delta_X^*\varepsilon_q}\Delta_X^*.$$
In particular we do not apply a Cartesian base-change theorem to this square. By (**) in step 3 the transpose of $\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ is $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$. This is exactly the transpose defining $\mu_f$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], so
$$\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f=\mu_f.$$
Also $\mu_f$ respects tensor symmetry: after transposition its two candidate composites are respectively $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$ followed by the symmetry and the symmetry followed by $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$, which agree by naturality of the symmetry. This comparison uses the ordinary adjunction of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1).

source.place: Evaluation, diagonal exchange and the multiplication claim

proof.text:
Take $\Delta_Y^*\dashv R\Delta_{Y*}$ adjoints, using [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). By the definitions of evaluation kernels and $\rho_f$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], the adjoint of the left side of (1) is
$$\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_{K'}(1\otimes\chi_f)\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f^{-1},\qquad
\overline{\mathrm{ev}}=\mathrm{ev}\circ\mathrm{sym}.$$
Naturality of the ordinary counit identifies the adjoint of the right side with $\tau_f\,Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\,\mathrm{Ex}$. Precompose both arrows with the isomorphism $\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$. Step 4 changes the second arrow into $\tau_f Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\mu_f$. The tensor--Hom transpose defining $\chi_f$, and the symmetry compatibility of $\mu_f$ just checked, give
$$\tau_f Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\mu_f
=\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_{K'}(1\otimes\chi_f).$$
Cancel $\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ and use injectivity of the diagonal adjunction bijection. This proves (1).

source.place: Evaluation (1), final diagonal and tensor--Hom adjunctions

proof.text: For support, the two fixed squares are Cartesian by [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian]. Since $X$ and $Y$ are separated, their diagonals are closed immersions by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Their base changes $i_c,i_b$ are closed immersions by [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image]. Thus $\Delta_X,\Delta_Y,i_c,i_b$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and their compact-support direct images agree with their ordinary direct images by [prop-functor-package](3). The maps $g$ and $f$ are proper by the pushforward hypothesis, and $h,q$ are proper by [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. There is no properness assertion about $c,b,d_c,d_b$ or the structure maps.

source.place: Support (2), geometry of the two fixed squares

proof.text:
Apply step 2 to the fixed square, with $(\alpha,\alpha',\beta,\beta')=(\Delta_X,i_c,c,d_c)$. The inverse right-adjoint fixed-square base change is the map used to define $\zeta_c$ by [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] and [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. The canonical functorial dualizing identification of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] gives $Rd_c^!\omega_X\cong\omega_{F_c}$. Thus the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_c$ is
$$Rc_!Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong Rc_!Ri_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X
 \cong R\Delta_{X!}Rd_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X
 \xrightarrow{R\Delta_{X!}\varepsilon_{d_c}}R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X.$$
For $b$, the parameters in step 2 are $(\Delta_Y,i_b,b,d_b)$, with proper $\Delta_Y,i_b$ by step 6. The definition of $\zeta_b$ and the dualizing comparison $Rd_b^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_{F_b}$ therefore give its exceptional adjoint as
$$Rb_!Ri_{b*}\omega_{F_b}
 \cong Rb_!Ri_{b!}Rd_b^!\omega_Y
 \cong R\Delta_{Y!}Rd_{b!}Rd_b^!\omega_Y
 \xrightarrow{R\Delta_{Y!}\varepsilon_{d_b}}R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y.$$
The two displayed maps retain $Rd_{c!}$ and $Rd_{b!}$; neither fixed-locus projection was assumed proper.

source.place: Support (2), exceptional adjoints of the support isomorphisms

proof.text:
Take the $Rb_!\dashv Rb^!$ adjoints of both sides of (2). The adjunction is the specified one of [def-trf-admissibility]. For the left side, the defining transpose of $\mathsf E$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] says
$$\varepsilon_b\,Rb_!\mathsf E=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\,\Xi.$$
Counit naturality therefore gives
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\;Rq_*\bigl(\varepsilon_c\,Rc_!\zeta_c\bigr)\;\Xi.$$
Insert step 7. The source identifies, using properness of $g,i_c,q,\Delta_X,f$ and the composition law, with
$$Rb_!Rg_*Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong Rq_*R\Delta_{X*}Rd_{c!}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong R\Delta_{Y*}Rf_*Rd_{c!}\omega_{F_c}.$$
The arrow under this identification is
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\tau_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{d_c}\bigr).$$
By the pasted-counit calculation in step 1 and the functorial dualizing identifications of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], the inner map is the counit of $R(fd_c)_!\dashv R(fd_c)^!$ at $\omega_Y$, with source $R(fd_c)_!\omega_{F_c}$.

For the right side of (2), first insert $Ri_{b*}\tau_h$ and then take the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_b$ found in step 7. Its value is
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\varepsilon_{d_b}\circ Rd_{b!}\tau_h\bigr),$$
with source identified as $R\Delta_{Y*}Rd_{b!}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}$. Here $\tau_h$ is precisely the exceptional counit after the dualizing identification by [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Thus step 1 identifies the inner composite with the counit for $d_bh$ at $\omega_Y$. The defining equalities $i_bh=gi_c$ and $d_bh=fd_c$ of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] identify this source with that in step 8 and this counit with the one in step 8. The two identifications agree by the associative composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and its adjoint normalization from step 1; the dualizing comparisons agree by functoriality in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. Therefore the exceptional adjoints, and hence the original maps, agree. This proves (2), using only the two fixed squares as Cartesian squares.

split_report.summary: Expanded all three blueprint calculations into nine steps. Retained compact support along the possibly nonproper fixed-locus projections, corrected the improper identification of compact-support and ordinary exchange, cited the kernel definitions explicitly, supplied the geometry for the fixed immersions, and used constructible adjunctions instead of the stronger ambient hypothesis of the old mate lemma. No new nodes. Second reader specified the four product factors and complete inverse Künneth composite, cited finite-Tor dual preservation, displayed both support transposes, and expanded hypothesis-bearing citation quotes. The open-factor normalization is checked by the restriction equations for the normalized proper/open comparison and ordinary base change.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 proof: last-assertion paragraph -> steps 1–2; Evaluation (1) -> steps 3–5; Support (2) -> steps 6–9. These realize unit sk-p-proper steps 3 (second kernel calculation) and 4 (support calculation).

tool_uses.why: The normalized proper/open comparison and its base-change equation verify the open factor in the explicit double-transpose calculation; this is the generic compact-support construction tool.
Stability of properness under arbitrary base change for the auxiliary square and product factors; a generic scheme tool, not a replacement for a trace calculation.
Only its closed-immersion stability clause is used for the two fixed immersions; no node of this unit supplies that generic geometry.
Closed immersions are proper, to compare shriek and star at diagonals and fixed inclusions; a generic scheme tool.
Its identity normalization on the open checks the open-factor counit equation; this is an extension-by-zero tool, not a trace-compatibility theorem.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-c41e3115d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all nine steps and every cited statement. The item statement matches the main-20261015 blueprint word for word, with no weakening. The base-change morphism in the 'Moreover' clause is the conjugate of Ex_! under the composite adjunctions, of type Ralpha'_*Rbeta'^! -> Rbeta^!Ralpha_*. That agrees with def-trf-admissibility, fix-prop-adjunctions(4) and thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change(2), and zeta_c is its inverse's inverse. All work is at the finite stage A_{E,n} in D^b_ctf. Steps I re-derived myself: the double transpose and (*), with the proper factor done by the mate identity and the open factor done by injective restriction (extension by zero is fully faithful) plus e∘j^*gamma=id and j'^*epsilon_alpha=epsilon_alpha'∘alpha'^*e; (**) from the exact composite in thm-sf-kunneth-relative over B=YxY, giving r^*eps_a ⊗ t^*eps_b and eps_q=eps_t∘t^*eps_b; Ex∘Delta_Y^*Pi_f=mu_f; the chi_f/ev-bar identity; the support adjoints through E's defining transpose, the step-7 adjoints and associativity of compact-support composition. Geometry checks: X and Y are separated, so the diagonals and i_c, i_b are closed immersions, hence proper; h and q are proper by lem-trf-fixed-map-proper. The two blueprint errors the delivery corrects are real: beta need not be proper (A1 -> Spec k), and d_b need not be proper (Y=Spec k, D=A1). Small cases checked: beta=id, alpha=id, f=g=id, empty fixed schemes. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses; there is no cycle (the id in def-exchange-projection is only a citers entry) and no merged or missing dependency. The only off-route node is lem-trf-open-square-exchange, declared in tool_uses; I accept it, and the other declared tool uses fit. thm-sf-dual-base-change states only existence, so it is not a duplicate.
